raw_response:
I'm 73 this year. My legs ache when the weather changes, but I've been working these fields since I was 18, and I still know every corner of my 4.1 mu. I only finished primary school — I can read prices at the shop and write my name, but I don't bother with those thick agricultural pamphlets the extension office prints. I learn by watching my neighbors and remembering what happened on my own land.

Seven people in my house. My son and daughter-in-law work at a factory in town, so it's mostly me and my old wife in the fields, with the grandchildren helping when school is out. We don't have much cash. I keep about 2,500 yuan put aside for farm inputs this year, and I don't borrow — at my age, owing money keeps me awake at night.

I spread my risks. I put 2 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, 1.5 mu in cotton, and the remaining 0.6 mu in stevia that my nephew talked me into trying two years ago. Every crop gets what it needs, but cotton gets the most attention because it brings the most cash.

The wheat went in last October, same as always. I used the common local seed, about 20 jin per mu, and put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base. Now it's spring, and the wheat is greening up. I'll topdress with about 20 jin of urea per mu at jointing — I walk past old Zhang's field every morning, and if his wheat looks greener than mine, I add a handful more. I'll irrigate twice more: once at jointing and once when the grain is filling. The well has meters now, so water costs money — I don't waste it. One spray of herbicide in March should handle the weeds. I expect about 400 jin per mu, maybe 450 if the spring stays moist.

Cotton goes in mid-April, around Qingming. I buy improved seed from the agricultural shop — the same kind my neighbor Li used last year, and his cotton looked strong. About 4 jin per mu. I plough and make beds in April, then put down base fertilizer: one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. When the cotton flowers in July, I'll topdress with another 15-20 jin of urea. The bollworm is my main worry — I'll spray insecticide three or four times this summer. I irrigate twice, maybe three times if July turns dry. Picking is all by hand, done by me and my wife over September and October. It's back-breaking work, but machine picking costs money we don't have. I hope for 250 jin of lint per mu.

Maize gets planted on the same 2 mu right after we cut the wheat in early June. That window is tight — sometimes only five or six days. I hire a small tractor to rotary-till and plant, costs me 50 yuan per mu but saves my back at my age. I use hybrid seed, about 5 jin per mu. One shot of compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 jin per mu. If the summer rains come, I might not irrigate at all, but usually I need to water once in July. Maize mostly grows itself after that. Should get 450 to 500 jin per mu.

Stevia is on the remaining 0.6 mu. I transplant seedlings in May. It doesn't need much — half a bag of compound fertilizer and that's it for the season. I water it more often but lightly. Harvest twice, once in July and once before frost in September. The medicine buyers pay decent money for the dried leaves, but it's a small plot so it only brings a few hundred yuan. Every bit helps.

My wife and I do almost all the labor ourselves. The only hired work is the tractor for maize planting. We don't hire pickers — can't afford them. If fertilizer prices go up, I just use less and accept slightly lower yields. Last year my neighbor bought some fancy new seed and had germination problems, so I'm sticking with what I know. At 73, I don't experiment much anymore. I just need steady, decent harvests to get through the year.
